changes.text: The rail toggle has the static name "Sidebar" and reports its state with `aria-expanded` (was "Expand sidebar" / "Collapse sidebar" with `aria-pressed`).
Degraded and down status is no longer colour-only: every item with `status: 'deg'` or `'down'` carries a visually hidden `, degraded` / `, down` word next to the dot.
Section label and sub-list ids are unique per instance (were `ss-side-sec-*` / `ss-side-sub-*`), so two sidebars on one page no longer share ids.
The layout mirrors under `dir="rtl"`: borders, margins, padding and text alignment use logical properties, and the open disclosure caret still points down.

`SideItem.external` (with `href`) renders the item as a new-tab link: `target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, a trailing external glyph (`.ext`) and an "(opens in a new tab)" announcement, also folded into the collapsed-rail name.
Link items no longer show the global animated `a::before` underline from `theme.css`; the reset also ships in `vanilla.css`.
The active item's tint is mixed from `--ss-accent` with `color-mix()` instead of reading `--ss-primary-rgb`.
The gap between an item's icon and label reads the spacing token `--ss-s-2` instead of a hardcoded `8px` (visually unchanged).
The rail fills its host container's height (`min-height: 100%`), so its border and background span the full column instead of stopping at the last item.

The root is a `<nav aria-label="Sidebar">` (was `<aside>`) and each group renders as a `<ul class="list">` of `<li class="row">` labelled by its section heading, so assistive tech hears item counts and hierarchy.
`SideItem.href` renders the item as a real `<a href>` with `aria-current="page"` when active; `onSelect` still fires and stays the fallback for items without `href`.

Collapsible icon-only rail: `collapsed` hides labels and section text (`data-collapsed` on the root) and `onToggleCollapsed` renders a built-in toggle button. Collapsed items get an `aria-label` and `title` with the label, status and badge.
`SideItem.children` renders one level of nested items as a disclosure (`aria-expanded` / `aria-controls`), opened automatically when a child is active.
`SideItem.badge` (`string | number`) renders a square count next to the status dot and is included in the accessible name.

New size-aware tokens `--ss-side-w`, `--ss-side-w-rail`, `--ss-side-badge-py` and `--ss-side-badge-px` set the expanded and rail widths and the badge padding. The `SideItem`, `SideGroup` and `SideStatus` types are exported from the package.
`SideItem.icon` is optional; omit it for a text-only item.
Styles are scoped to the component and ship with it instead of living in the global `theme.css`.
`size` prop (`sm` | `md` | `lg`), rendered as `data-size-variant` on the root; it inherits the global size when unset.
Accessibility pass: the root has `aria-label="Sidebar"`, the active item has `aria-current="page"`, items activate with Space as well as Enter, and the status dot is `aria-hidden`.
The item hover background reads `--ss-hover` instead of a hardcoded white tint, so it is visible on the light theme.
The root class is `ss-side` (was `hub-side`), part of the global `hub-` → `ss-` class and `--hs-*` → `--ss-*` token rename.

New component: a vertical navigation rail of sectioned items (`groups`), each with an icon, a label and an optional status dot (`up` | `deg` | `down`), with `active` marking the current item and `onSelect` firing on click or Enter.
